docs.title: TermForge
docs.text:
A universal terminal UI/UX design system for Python.

Build beautiful, themed terminal interfaces with a single import. No Rich types in your signatures. Pure functions. Zero boilerplate.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.CardSpec(title="Server Node-01", content="CPU: 42%\nRAM: 8.2 GB")))
print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="ACTIVE", severity="success")))
print(tf.draw(tf.ProgressSpec(progress=0.85, width=30)))

docs.title: Why TermForge?
docs.text:
• Single import — import termforge as tf gives you everything
  • Declarative specs — JSON-serializable component specs, renderers are pure functions
  • 6 built-in themes — Catppuccin Mocha, Dracula, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbox, High Contrast
  • 30+ components — cards, charts, tables, trees, dialogs, animations, and more
  • Color-depth fallback — truecolor to 256 to 16 to monochrome, automatic
  • CLI tools — demo, playground REPL, layout visualizer, benchmark

docs.title: tf.draw(spec, width=80, height=24, theme=None, depth=None) -> str
docs.text:
Render any component spec to a printable multi-line string.

import termforge as tf
print(tf.draw(tf.CardSpec(title="Hi", content="Hello")))

docs.title: tf.render(spec, width=80, height=24, theme=None, depth=None) -> list[str]
docs.text:
Render any component spec to a list of ANSI-formatted strings (one per row).

lines = tf.render(tf.CardSpec(title="Hi", content="Hello"), width=50, height=6)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Name Type Default Description spec RenderableSpec — Any component spec (e.g. CardSpec) width int 80 Canvas width in columns height int 24 Canvas height in rows theme ThemeTokens \| None None Theme tokens; defaults to Tokyo Night depth ColorDepth \| None None Color depth; auto-detected if None

docs.title: Default Theme
docs.text:
When theme is None, TermForge uses Tokyo Night. To obtain those tokens explicitly:

from termforge.core.theme import load_theme_from_dict, TOKYO_NIGHT
theme = load_theme_from_dict(TOKYO_NIGHT)

docs.title: Specs
docs.text: All specs follow the pattern tf.<Name>Spec(...) and expose .to_dict() / .from_dict() for JSON serialization. Refer to each component's section in Components for field details.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
from termforge.core.capability import detect_capabilities
caps = detect_capabilities()
print(caps.color_depth)  # auto-detected terminal color depth

docs.title: Themes
docs.text: TermForge ships 6 built-in themes.

docs.title: Available Themes
docs.text: Theme Key Style Catppuccin Mocha catppuccin_mocha Pastel dark Dracula dracula High-contrast dark Tokyo Night tokyo_night Blue-toned dark Nord nord Arctic cool Gruvbox gruvbox Warm retro High Contrast high_contrast Accessibility

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import termforge as tf
from termforge.theme.builtin import BUILTIN_THEMES

theme = BUILTIN_THEMES["catppuccin_mocha"].tokens
print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="OK", severity="success"), theme=theme))

docs.title: Default Theme
docs.text:
Tokyo Night is applied automatically when no theme is provided. You can also build its tokens directly:

from termforge.core.theme import load_theme_from_dict, TOKYO_NIGHT

theme = load_theme_from_dict(TOKYO_NIGHT)

docs.title: Custom Themes
docs.text:
Themes are plain dicts loaded via load_theme_from_dict:

from termforge.core.theme import load_theme_from_dict

my_theme = load_theme_from_dict({
    "colors": {
        "primary": [100, 200, 255],
        "secondary": [180, 150, 255],
        # ...
    }
})

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
TermForge ships 30+ terminal UI components. All are:

  • Spec-based — create a spec object, pass it to a renderer
  • Themeable — accept an optional theme: ThemeTokens
  • Serializable — all specs have .to_dict() / .from_dict()
  • Pure functions — renderers return list[str], no side effects

docs.title: Usage Pattern
docs.text:
import termforge as tf

# 1. Create a spec
spec = tf.CardSpec(title="My Card", content="Hello world")

# 2. Render via tf.draw() (easiest) — returns a printable string
print(tf.draw(spec))

# 3. Or render via tf.render() for a list of lines
lines = tf.render(spec, width=50, height=8)

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
• Display — Card, Badge, Text, Toast, Tooltip, Divider
  • Input — ButtonGroup, Checklist, Combobox, Radio, Slider, Toggle, SearchBar
  • Layout — Windows, Panes, Dialog, Accordion, Tabs
  • Charts — Line, Bar, Scatter, Sparkline, Heatmap, Candlestick

docs.title: Charts
docs.text: All charts use a single tf.ChartSpec, selecting a renderer via the tf.ChartType enum. Data is passed in series (or ohlc_series for candlesticks).

docs.title: ChartType
docs.text:
Type Enum value Line ChartType.LINE Bar ChartType.BAR Scatter ChartType.SCATTER Sparkline ChartType.SPARKLINE Heatmap ChartType.HEATMAP Candlestick ChartType.CANDLESTICK

Also available: HISTOGRAM, STACKED_BAR, MULTI_BAR.

docs.title: Line
docs.text:
import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ChartSpec(
    chart_type=tf.ChartType.LINE,
    series=[[3, 7, 2, 8, 5, 9, 4, 6]],
    width=48,
    height=10,
    title="Requests/sec",
), width=48, height=10))

docs.title: Sparkline
docs.text:
A compact single-line trend.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ChartSpec(
    chart_type=tf.ChartType.SPARKLINE,
    series=[[1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 7]],
    width=24,
), width=24))

docs.title: Heatmap
docs.text:
import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ChartSpec(
    chart_type=tf.ChartType.HEATMAP,
    series=[[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]],

docs.title: Candlestick
docs.text:
Candlesticks use ohlc_series, an OHLCSeries whose data is a list of {"open", "high", "low", "close"} dicts.

import termforge as tf

ohlc = tf.OHLCSeries(data=[
    {"open": 10, "high": 13, "low": 9, "close": 12},
    {"open": 12, "high": 14, "low": 11, "close": 11},
    {"open": 11, "high": 12, "low": 10, "close": 11},
])
print(tf.draw(tf.ChartSpec(
    chart_type=tf.ChartType.CANDLESTICK,
    ohlc_series=ohlc,
    width=40,
    height=12,
), width=40, height=12))

docs.title: Display Components
docs.text: Components for presenting information. Each example builds a spec and renders it with tf.draw().

docs.title: Card
docs.text:
A bordered panel with an optional title, subtitle, and body content.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.CardSpec(
    title="Server Node-01",
    subtitle="us-east-1",
    content="CPU: 42%\nRAM: 8.2 GB\nStatus: healthy",
    width=36,
)))

docs.title: Badge
docs.text:
A compact status label with a severity color.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="ACTIVE", severity="success")))
print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="DEGRADED", severity="warning")))
print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="OFFLINE", severity="error")))

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Aligned, wrapped text with overflow control.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.TextSpec(
    content="TermForge renders rich text with alignment and wrapping.",
    align="center",
    max_width=40,
), width=40))

docs.title: Toast
docs.text:
A transient notification bubble.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ToastSpec(text="File saved successfully", toast_type="success")))

docs.title: Tooltip
docs.text:
A pointer bubble anchored to a coordinate.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.TooltipSpec(text="Press Enter to confirm", anchor_x=4, anchor_y=0)))

docs.title: Divider
docs.text:
A horizontal rule with an optional centered label.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.DividerSpec(label="SETTINGS", alignment="center", width=40), width=40))

docs.title: Input Components
docs.text: Components that represent interactive controls. Specs are stateless — you hold selection state (e.g. selected_idx) in your own application and re-render on change.

docs.title: ButtonGroup
docs.text:
A horizontal row of buttons with one selected.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ButtonGroupSpec(
    buttons=["Save", "Cancel", "Reset"],
    selected_idx=0,
)))

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
A multi-item list with checked/unchecked state and a cursor.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ChecklistSpec(
    items=[
        tf.ChecklistItemSpec(label="Enable logging", checked=True),
        tf.ChecklistItemSpec(label="Verbose output", checked=False),
    ],
    selected_idx=0,
)))

docs.title: Combobox
docs.text:
A single-select dropdown.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ComboboxSpec(
    options=["Python", "Rust", "Go"],
    selected_idx=0,
    is_open=True,
)))

docs.title: Radio
docs.text:
A single-select group of options.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.RadioButtonSpec(
    items=[
        tf.RadioButtonItemSpec(label="Light"),
        tf.RadioButtonItemSpec(label="Dark"),
    ],
    selected_idx=1,
)))

docs.title: Slider
docs.text:
A value slider between a min and max.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.SliderSpec(value=65, min_val=0, max_val=100, label="Volume", width=40), width=40))

docs.title: Toggle
docs.text:
An on/off switch.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.ToggleSwitchSpec(label="Dark mode", state=True)))

docs.title: SearchBar
docs.text:
A query field with filtered candidates.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.SearchBarSpec(
    query="dra",
    candidates=["dracula", "gruvbox", "nord"],
    placeholder="Search themes...",
)))

docs.title: Layout Components
docs.text: Components for structuring the screen — windows, split panes, dialogs, and collapsible sections.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
A bordered, titled region with scrollable content.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.WindowSpec(
    title="Logs",
    content="[12:00] boot complete\n[12:01] listening on :8080",
    width=48,
    height=6,
), width=48, height=6))

docs.title: Panes
docs.text:
Split layouts that compose child windows horizontally or vertically.

import termforge as tf

left = tf.WindowSpec(title="Nav", content="Home\nDocs\nAbout")
right = tf.WindowSpec(title="Content", content="Welcome to TermForge")

pane = tf.PaneSpec(direction="horizontal", children=[left, right], ratios=[1, 2])
print(tf.draw(pane, width=60, height=8))

docs.title: Dialog
docs.text:
A modal prompt with a title, body, and focusable buttons.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.DialogSpec(
    title="Confirm",
    body="Delete this file? This cannot be undone.",
    buttons=["Cancel", "Delete"],
    focused_button_index=1,
), width=48, height=8))

docs.title: Accordion
docs.text:
A vertical list of collapsible sections.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.AccordionSpec(
    items=[
        tf.AccordionItemSpec(title="General", details="Theme, language", is_expanded=True),
        tf.AccordionItemSpec(title="Advanced", details="Flags, env vars"),
    ],
    selected_idx=0,
)))

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
A horizontal tab strip with one active tab.

import termforge as tf

print(tf.draw(tf.TabSpec(titles=["Overview", "Metrics", "Logs"], active_index=1), width=48))

docs.title: Requirements

  • pyyaml >= 6.0 (declarative config)

import termforge as tf

# Render a card
print(tf.draw(tf.CardSpec(title="Hello", content="Welcome to TermForge!")))

docs.title: Using Themes
docs.text:
import termforge as tf
from termforge.theme.builtin import BUILTIN_THEMES

# Load a theme (keys: catppuccin_mocha, dracula, tokyo_night, nord, gruvbox, high_contrast)
theme = BUILTIN_THEMES["catppuccin_mocha"].tokens

# Apply it to any component
print(tf.draw(tf.BadgeSpec(text="SUCCESS", severity="success"), theme=theme))

specs = load_config_yaml("layout.yaml")
